children: There's a perfect storm of three factors hitting bitcoin all at once, analysts from Yield Basis say in a research note. For one, investors now expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December, making yieldless assets more expensive to hold, they say. Secondly, there is a selloff in AI stocks that is forcing funds to decrease their risks, the analysts say. And lastly, bitcoin fell below its 200-day average, causing more than $2 billion of long positions to be forcibly closed out over the weekend, they say. On top of all that, there are concerns that AI and quantum computing could break encryption, which is tough for crypto's underdeveloped defenses, the analysts say. Bitcoin is down 1.7% at $62,830. (dean.seal@wsj.com)
